concept.name: Mode
concept.definition: The value that occurs with the greatest frequency in a data set, or the location of the peak of a probability distribution. A distribution may have one mode (unimodal), several modes (multimodal), or no well-defined mode.
concept.intuition: It is the most common outcome - the value you would bet on if you had to guess exactly one number.
concept.mechanics: For discrete data, count frequencies and select the most frequent value; for continuous data, values essentially never repeat, so the mode is taken as the peak of a histogram or density estimate (e.g., the midpoint of the tallest histogram bin).
concept.failure_modes: For continuous data the sample mode is unstable and depends on histogram binning, and multimodal data make 'the mode' ambiguous. The mode ignores all non-peak values, so it carries no information about spread or tails.
concept.misconceptions: The mode is not the same as the mean or median and is not necessarily near the center of the data - in a right-skewed distribution it sits below both. A data set can legitimately have more than one mode or none.
concept.example: For a normal sample the mean, median, and mode nearly coincide, while for a lognormal sample NIST reports mode 0.68, median 0.99, mean 1.68 - the mode sits at the peak of the right-skewed density.
